Query:
WITH ranked AS (
 SELECT id,account_id,kind,
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY ts DESC,id DESC) AS rn
 FROM events WHERE ts<=:cutoff AND kind<>'void'
)
SELECT a.id AS account,
 COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.label='active' AND e.kind='credit' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS credit_total,
 COUNT(e.id) AS joined_events, COUNT(DISTINCT t.label) AS tag_kinds,
 r.id AS latest_event, r.kind AS latest_kind
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.account_id=a.id AND e.ts<=:cutoff
LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.account_id=a.id
LEFT JOIN ranked r ON r.account_id=a.id AND r.rn=1
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
 SELECT 1 FROM bans b WHERE b.account_id=a.id AND b.reason='hold'
 AND b.since<=:cutoff AND (b.until IS NULL OR b.until>:cutoff)
)
GROUP BY a.id,r.id,r.kind ORDER BY a.id

1. Determine account eligibility and the latest eligible event per account, respecting the cutoff, ban reason, exclusive endpoints and ordering ties.
2. Evaluate the joins and aggregates with bag multiplicities and SQL NULL semantics; combine every eligible account into the result.

Apply this closed-world async job-state specification. No external observations are needed.
Rules: Each job starts at epoch 0, state absent, owner null, result null. Events apply in supplied order. submit(job,v): only v greater than the current epoch resets the job to queued at epoch v, owner/result null; otherwise ignore. claim(job,v,w): only the current epoch in queued state becomes running with owner w. transfer(job,v,from,to): only current epoch, running state, and matching from owner replaces the owner with to; otherwise ignore. cancel(job,v): only current epoch; queued becomes cancelled, running becomes cancel_requested; all other states are unchanged. finish(job,v,w,value): only current epoch, matching owner, and state running or cancel_requested commits the value and changes state to committed, owner null. A request without its acknowledgement does not prevent finish. ack_cancel(job,v,w): only current epoch, matching owner, and state cancel_requested becomes cancelled, owner/result null. Other events are ignored. Terminal states ignore claim/cancel/finish/ack_cancel; a later higher-epoch submit can reset them. A stale epoch, wrong owner, duplicate submit or unsolicited acknowledgement grants no authority.
